resale_co.name: Certificate of Continuing Occupancy (Certificate of Occupancy for Resale)
resale_co.issued_by: City of Garfield Building Department (Construction Official as enforcement officer), with inspection by the Garfield Fire Prevention Bureau
resale_co.lead_time: The code gives the City up to 30 days after a complete application to inspect and issue the certificate. The City says not to schedule a closing until the C.O. is obtained.
requirements: General inspection of the visible parts of the building for imminent hazards and compliance with building, health, safety and fire codes
Approved smoke detector installed (smoke and carbon monoxide certification is done at the same time)
Seller and buyer names, current home addresses, phone numbers and emails (no business, attorney or realtor addresses)
For an estate sale, a copy of the Surrogate letter
If illegal extra units are found, separate utility services must be removed and the owner and buyer must sign a sworn statement

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online through the City's FastTrackGov citizen portal (create an account, submit and pay), or email Elizabeth Pacyga (epacyga@garfieldnj.org) with the property address, the buyer's and seller's names, home addresses, phones and emails, and the Surrogate letter for an estate. Wait for the City's email before paying; pay the C.O. fee by check or money order to "CITY OF GARFIELD" and the smoke certification fee separately to "BUREAU OF FIRE PREVENTION".
resale_co.contact_title: Named on the City's resale C.O. instructions as the person to start the process

resale_co.notes: Garfield Code Chapter 105 (Certificates of Continued Occupancy) was read through ecode360; Section 105-9 fees (amended 2022 and 2023) match the City's resale instruction sheet. The Fire Prevention page also names Debra Schult (dschult@garfieldnj.org) for information on C.O. and smoke/CO inspections. Garfield also has a separate Dwelling Certificate law (Chapter 128) that requires an inspection before transfer of title of a one- or two-unit dwelling; see other_items. Rental dwelling certificate inspections for 1-2 family rentals are a rental program and are mentioned only for context.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and outside each separate sleeping area, located per NFPA 72
Battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units (UL 217); hardwired alarms must stay hardwired
Carbon monoxide alarms in the immediate vicinity of sleeping areas (UL 2034), where there is a fuel-burning device or attached garage
Smoke and CO detectors within 10 feet of all bedrooms; access to the attic and basement at the inspection
Fire extinguisher (an older City smoke detector application form still lists it)

fire_cert.notes: The City's resale instruction sheet gives smoke/CO certification fees of $50.00 (1 family) and $100.00 (2 family). An older posted Smoke Detector Application form (naming former Fire Official Gerald Walis) shows tiered fees of $35.00, $70.00 and $125.00 by business days before the change of occupant and still lists a fire extinguisher; it looks outdated, so those tiers are not used here. The state dropped the extinguisher from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19). The Dwelling Certificate fee in Code Section 128 ($60 per unit) says it includes the smoke detector certification, which may overlap with these fees; confirm with the City.

other_items.label: Dwelling certificate before transfer of title
other_items.detail: Garfield Code Chapter 128 requires a dwelling certificate (number of occupants and unit location) filed not more than 60 days before conveyance of a one- or two-unit dwelling, with a dwelling inspection before transfer of title, unless one was done within 11 months. The code fee is $60 per dwelling unit, which it says includes the smoke detector certification; a $60 return-visit fee applies if access is not given.

open_questions: Is the Chapter 128 dwelling certificate ($60 per unit) charged on a sale in addition to the resale C.O. and smoke certification, or is it combined?
Is the old tiered smoke detector fee ($35/$70/$125) still used, or only the flat $50/$100 on the resale sheet?
Is a fire extinguisher still checked at resale after P.L.2025, c.19?
How long is the resale C.O. valid, and what is the usual turnaround?
